consensus_summary: Primary consensus meaning of lamp oil is the Holy Spirit (indwelling/anointing/empowering presence), drawn especially from Matt 25:1–13, Zech 4, tabernacle lamp oil, and anointing texts; common alternatives are good works/charity, grace, true faith or preparedness/watchfulness, with minority readings of the Word of God or joy; no fully settled cross-traditional consensus.
book_summary: The commandment's truth and correction received and laid up inwardly until they govern the life—the tested, pressed fruit of the Spirit stored as proven obedience; light is that obedience made visible as an example to others.
rationale: The book's definition is compatible with the consensus (which centers the Spirit and includes works, inner spiritual reality, and minority Word associations) yet materially sharper and more synthetic: it reframes oil specifically as internalized commandment-truth/correction that becomes the Spirit's tested fruit in the form of governing obedience, with light as the resulting visible example. This narrows and precises the broader Spirit/works/faith alternatives without flatly contradicting them.
strongest_objection: Dominant tradition (and the book's own common-view note) treats lamp oil as the Holy Spirit itself rather than its fruit or stored commandments; the synthesis risks over-allegorizing Matt 25 beyond readiness while subordinating direct Spirit texts (Zech 4, anointings) to a Word-and-obedience scheme.
